Fix council seat readiness so it accepts every model id a gateway advertises, not
only the displayed one.

reported unavailable. The observable symptom is that `kbu council doctor` reports
the WHOLE ARGO bench unavailable and every ARGO seat is refused at submit, while
the call itself would have succeeded.

all from `main` today.

entry advertises -- at minimum `id`, `internal_id` and `name` -- so a readiness
match on any advertised spelling succeeds. Do not special-case ARGO by name or
URL: a gateway carrying more than one spelling per model is a general shape, and
MAG also advertises provider-suffixed ids. Keep the matching normalisation
(case, whitespace) that is already there if any; add tests for the multi-spelling
case.

IMPORTANT CONTEXT YOU SHOULD KNOW AND NOT BE CONFUSED BY. An equivalent fix
exists as commit 0825c5a in an h100-local clone and in NO shared branch -- the
object is not even present in the shared repo, so you cannot cherry-pick it and
must not try. Implement the fix fresh with tests. Once this lands, that local
commit is superseded and should be discarded rather than left as a second
divergent fix; say so in your work record.

matches; and a seat naming a spelling the gateway does not advertise is still
reported unavailable. The tests this task adds pass, and no test that passed on
the base commit fails on the branch.

Build the token model the quote is based on: a fit, from the council store's own
measured history, of input tokens per prompt character and mean output tokens,
per (seat, role).

    fit_token_model(store, *, seats) -> TokenModel

reading `attempts.usage` (JSON, per-attempt token counts) and `calls.fresh_usage`
for every successful call belonging to each named seat and role. For each
(seat, role) pair report:
  - input tokens per prompt character, fitted over the available attempts
  - mean and an upper band (use a high percentile, not mean+k*sd -- the
    distributions are skewed by long candidate menus) for output tokens
  - the SAMPLE SIZE, carried through to the caller

no single tokenizer is correct across it, and carrying three would be a
dependency for each. We have ~58,000 real calls per chair with recorded token
counts, which is better calibrated than any third-party tokenizer and costs
nothing. The prior run's per-item projection was accurate to 1.4% off a far

and a fallback drawn from the measured per-seat figures in the background section
above -- never silently zero, and never silently borrowed from a different seat.

Also expose `kbu council token-model [--json]` so an operator can see the fit and
its sample sizes.

we do for a specific task, and this should go into the hash. The thing I think

are best able to allocate token cost."

    {query: "<name>@<version>", bench_fingerprint: "<sha>", mapping_hash: "<sha>"}

    canonical_sha256([{role, canonical_model} for role, seat in roster.seats()])

covers role, endpoint_kind, model (the route spelling), canonical_model,
max_output_tokens, temperature and extra -- so it INCLUDES THE TRANSPORT. Moving
a seat from the codex CLI to MAG changes it, which would re-partition all 47,341
clearinghouse functions and re-charge ~199M tokens for a pure cost optimisation.

roster_fingerprint and the per-seat route_fingerprint are still RECORDED as
provenance on every row; they are simply not partition keys. route_fingerprint's
own docstring says it "answers 'where did this come from', not 'is this the same
question'".

temperature, max_output_tokens and extra are DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from
bench_fingerprint: they are substantially transport-coupled, so including them
would let a routing change re-partition the corpus through the back door.

(types.py:264) KEEPS endpoint_kind. Do not "fix" it to match. Its docstring's
reason holds and is measured: the same ~1,400-token question cost ~63,000 input
tokens over `claude -p` against 1,403 over the API, because the CLI path wraps an
agent harness around it. The partition key asks "is this the same experiment";
the reuse key asks "is this literally the same question already paid for".

`council/types.py` beside the existing fingerprints, documented so the three are
not confused (bench = partitions, roster = provenance, route = provenance).
Test that a transport-only change leaves it unchanged while a model change moves
it.
